Impact: affects any app trying to trigger a reactive side effect after a download completes; real but scoped to that specific pattern. No maintainer confirmation yet. Classification hypothesis: bug (narwhals column-access ambiguity for non-string column names). Duplicate check: distinct from #1844 (empty-string column name) -- different trigger and same subsystem but not the same defect; not marking duplicate. Wrong-location check: correct repo. Regression check: no prior-version comparison; not a regression. Reproduction plan: reporter's minimal example (DataFrame with columns=[0,1]) is directly runnable. Impact: workaround exists (rename columns to strings), so impact is moderate-to-low despite being a confusing failure mode. Priority: Low given the workaround and narrow trigger. title: Can not assign ID through @output(id=id) in render.download
rationale: Facts: weichisyu reports that using @output(id='download4') above @render.download(...) causes a 404 when the download link is clicked. Maintainer schloerke confirmed this reproduces on current main, extended the scope to also affect render.download_button/render.download_link, and traced the root cause to session._downloads being keyed by the output id at decoration time (before @output(id=...) renames it) while the download URL is computed lazily at render time using the renamed id, causing a dict-lookup miss; a workaround and a suggested fix are given. Classification hypothesis: bug, confirmed with detailed root cause. Duplicate check: none found. Wrong-location check: correct repo (confirmed this issue lives in posit-dev/py-shiny and concerns its own code, despite a stray comment about the docs-site repo). Regression check: no older-release comparison cited; not labeled regression. Reproduction plan: maintainer's reprex app with two download buttons is directly runnable. Impact: moderate -- silently broken downloads for any app using @output(id=...) to rename a download renderer's output id; a workaround exists. Priority: Medium. Recommended next action: label Priority: Medium and mark ai-triage:done; high confidence given full maintainer-confirmed root cause and reprex.

title: [bug] One-off behaviour of ui.update_slider() for datetime.date objects
rationale: Facts: danieldebondt-tf reports that ui.update_slider() with date values shifts the resulting slider dates by one day, suspecting a timezone/datetime-conversion issue. Maintainer schloerke reproduced it and traced the root cause precisely: _as_numeric() encodes a date as local midnight via datetime(y,m,d).timestamp(), while the client always reads/formats date-type sliders in UTC; for any positive-UTC-offset server timezone (all of Europe, most of Asia, Australia), local midnight is the previous UTC day, silently shifting both update_slider() and the initial input_slider() date value/min/max by one day. A standalone reprex without a browser, a full app-level reprex, and a suggested fix are all included. Classification hypothesis: bug, confirmed with thorough root cause and fix. Duplicate check: none found. Wrong-location check: correct repo (issue currently lives in posit-dev/py-shiny and concerns its own _input_slider.py). Regression check: no explicit older-release comparison is cited, so not labeled regression. Reproduction plan: the maintainer's standalone timezone-loop reprex and full app reprex are both directly runnable. Impact: high -- this silently produces incorrect dates (off by one) for any server running in a positive-UTC-offset timezone, affecting both initial slider values and updates, with no error or warning to alert developers. Priority: High given silent data-correctness impact at deployment scale, despite not being a security or production-outage issue. Recommended next action: label Priority: High and mark ai-triage:done; high confidence given full maintainer-confirmed root cause across timezones.
